n: On July 23, 1837—the very day the first missionaries began preaching in England—the Lord speaks to Thomas B. Marsh, President of the Quorum of the Twelve. His prayers and generosity for his fellow apostles have been noticed.

f.w: thine alms have come up as a memorial before me

f.g: Gifts to the poor or needy; acts of charity.

n: Gently but honestly, the Lord notes some things in Thomas’s heart that displeased him—possibly feelings about being passed over when Heber C. Kimball and Orson Hyde were sent to England.

f.w: some few things in thine heart
f.g: Thomas was reportedly upset that Joseph sent apostles to England without consulting him as quorum president.

n: Because Thomas has humbled himself, he will be lifted up, and his sins are forgiven.

f.w: abased thyself thou shalt be exalted

n: The Lord encourages Thomas: he will testify to Gentiles and Jews and send God’s word to the ends of the earth through the Twelve’s missionary work.
Thomas is to labor constantly, warning people morning and evening, so that his message keeps people awake spiritually.
He is to keep his home in Zion and not move away; the Lord has a great work for him.

f.g: Making known; proclaiming. Thomas was also involved in Church printing.

n: “Gird up thy loins” means get ready for action, as men tucked up long robes to run or work. Shod feet signal readiness to travel among mountains and nations.
Through his preaching, the proud will be humbled and the humble lifted up—a reversal often seen in scripture.

f.w: many high ones shall be brought low

n: His voice is to rebuke sin and silence slander.
One of the most loved verses in the Doctrine and Covenants: humility brings the Lord’s guiding hand and answers to prayer.
The Lord knows Thomas loves his quorum, but he should not love them more than others; his love should reach everyone who loves the Lord’s name.

f.w: let thy love abound unto all men

n: Thomas is to pray for the Twelve and correct them firmly. In 1837 several apostles were caught up in the dissent following the Kirtland bank’s failure.
After trials, the Lord will reach out to the apostles; if they stay soft-hearted, they will be converted and healed. Some of them later fell away; others returned.

f.g: An image of a stubborn ox resisting the yoke; to be stubborn or proud.

n: The message for Thomas applies to all the Twelve: get ready, take up the cross, follow Christ, and care for his flock—echoing Jesus’ charge to Peter.

f.w: take up your cross, follow me

n: A warning against pride and rebellion toward Joseph Smith, who holds keys that will remain with him until the Lord comes. Thomas Marsh himself left the Church the next year, returning in 1857.

f.w: rebel not against my servant Joseph
f.g: Several apostles, including Thomas B. Marsh in 1838, later turned against Joseph.

f.w: shall not be taken from him till I come

n: As President of the Twelve, Thomas held the keys of the kingdom for the Twelve’s work among the nations.
The Twelve were to open the work in places where the First Presidency—Joseph, Sidney, and Hyrum—could not personally go.

f.g: Hyrum Smith became a counselor in the First Presidency in November 1837, a few months after this revelation.

n: The First Presidency carried the burden of all the churches for the time being.

f.w: the burden of all the churches

n: Wherever the Presidency sends the Twelve, the Lord will be with them and open a door for the word to be received.

f.g: A real opportunity that leads to results.

n: Receiving Christ’s word means receiving him—and receiving the prophets he sends. The First Presidency are counselors to the Twelve.

f.w: Whosoever receiveth my word receiveth me

n: Missionaries sent by the Twelve, properly recommended and authorized, have power to open the kingdom to any nation.
Their power depends on humility, staying true to God’s word, and listening to the Spirit.

f.w: hearken to the voice of my Spirit

n: The Lord describes the spiritual condition of the world: darkness on the earth and deep darkness in people’s minds.

f.w: darkness covereth the earth, and gross darkness the minds of the people

n: Judgment is coming quickly—a day of burning, desolation, and mourning sweeping the earth like a whirlwind.
Sobering: judgment begins with the Lord’s own house—his Church—and then goes outward.

f.w: upon my house shall it begin

n: Especially those who claim to know the Lord but do not, and who blaspheme in the midst of his house. In 1837, apostasy in Kirtland was severe.
The Twelve are told not to get entangled in the troubled affairs of the Kirtland church, but to focus on their mission.

f.g: Kirtland, which was then torn by financial crisis and dissent.

n: First purify your hearts; then go preach to every creature who has not received the gospel.

f.w: preach my gospel unto every creature

n: Quoting Mark, the Lord restates the necessity of faith and baptism. “Damned” means stopped in progress, unable to receive the fullest blessings.

f.w: he that believeth and is baptized shall be saved

f.g: Condemned; in Latter-day Saint usage, halted in eternal progress.

n: The Twelve and First Presidency hold priesthood power for the last days—the dispensation of the fulness of times, when all past dispensations come together.

f.w: dispensation of the fulness of times

n: Their authority links them with every prophet who has held a dispensation since the creation.

f.w: from the beginning of the creation

n: These keys came down from the ancient fathers and were finally restored from heaven—by Peter, James, John, Moses, Elias, and Elijah.

f.w: being sent down from heaven unto you

n: The calling is great, so the Twelve must keep their hearts and lives clean, or they will be accountable for this generation.

f.w: Cleanse your hearts and your garments

n: Be faithful until the Lord returns; he will reward each person according to his works. Alpha and Omega—the first and last Greek letters—mean the Beginning and the End.
